observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly optimizes String(x) to x + '' even when x is not an immutable value, leading to incorrect JS output for objects or expressions with side effects.
hypothesis: The peephole optimization in PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax incorrectly replaces String(x) with x + '' without verifying that x is an immutable value. When x is an object or an expression with side effects, the conversion behavior of String(x) (which calls toString/valueOf) differs from the addition operator (which might call valueOf/toString in a different order or context), leading to incorrect results.
prediction: The code in PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax will lack a check for whether the argument to String() is an immutable value, and the fix will involve adding a condition to ensure only immutable values are optimized.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and the provided fix diff confirm that the optimization was applied too broadly. The fix adds a check (NodeUtil.isImmutableValue) to ensure the optimization is only applied when safe. This is a classic missing validation/guard error.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a missing guard condition in the peephole optimization logic. The compiler was performing a transformation that is only valid for immutable values on arbitrary expressions, which violates the semantics of the String() constructor in JavaScript. Adding the missing check for immutability corrects the logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a change to the algorithm itself, but the addition of a guard condition to prevent the algorithm from running in invalid cases.
